name: Arabidopsis radiation-quality classifier (OSD-46)
task: Three-class radiation quality classification from seedling expression
expressionUnits: log2 normalised Affymetrix intensities, gene-model collapsed by mean
method: logistic_l2 with in-fold ANOVA gene selection
validation: Leave-one-biological-group-out cross-validation over 22 groups. Gene filtering and ANOVA selection fitted inside each training fold only. Labels permuted between groups for the null.

bootstrapCi.method: stratified percentile bootstrap over held-out predictions

batchConfound.interpretation: Association between array processing batch and the class label. Gamma and HZE are balanced across batches; the control class is not.

domain.note: Supply log2 normalised expression for every gene in 'features'. Partial vectors are rejected rather than zero-filled.

referenceProfilesNote: Per-class mean of the training expression across the selected genes. These are class centroids computed from NASA OSD-46 data, NOT individual measured samples, and using one as model input is a synthetic input that must be labelled as such.
limitations: Ground-based irradiation of Arabidopsis seedlings, not spaceflight and not a crop.
Three discrete conditions from a single study; not a continuous dose-response surface.
100 Gy gamma and 30 Gy Fe-56 differ in BOTH quality and absorbed dose, so a classifier separating them cannot attribute the difference to radiation quality alone.
Gamma and HZE are balanced across array batches, so batch cannot explain this discrimination - but the control class is not batch-balanced.
The design is unbalanced: atm-1 lacks a 3 hour timepoint and controls carry no collection time.
Never predicts yield, biomass, survival or crop productivity; no such measurement exists in this study.
recommendedUse: Demonstrating that radiation quality leaves a recoverable molecular signature that generalises to held-out biological groups and across array batches. Not a dosimeter and not a crop-performance predictor.

phase10.explanationMethod: exact linear attribution of the served linear-softmax evaluator; the contributions reconstruct the served logits

license: Public OSDR access; retain study attribution and comply with OSDR terms; do not assume every contributed file is public domain.
sourceLicense: Public OSDR access; retain study attribution and comply with OSDR terms; do not assume every contributed file is public domain.
sourceCitation: NASA Open Science Data Repository, OSD-46: Gamma radiation and HZE treatment of seedlings in Arabidopsis (UC Davis / Brookhaven).
servedScope: Classification of the applied treatment (control / 100 Gy gamma / 30 Gy Fe-56) for Arabidopsis seedlings in OSD-46. Not a dose prediction, not a plant-health score, not a crop, and not spaceflight. Probabilities are measured, not calibrated, and the response reports the measurement.
note: No operational forecast. This card describes what the model reproduces inside the measured domain; it is not a prediction of a future or unmeasured crop.

probabilityCalibration.method: Leave-one-biological-group-out out-of-fold probabilities, the same split as the reported accuracy (recomputed and asserted equal). Log loss, Brier score and a 10-bin ECE were measured; a nested temperature search was run and reported.
probabilityCalibration.scope: Measured within OSD-46 only. It does not transfer to other radiation qualities, doses, organisms or platforms.
probabilityCalibration.statement: The class probabilities are uncalibrated scores from a regularised logistic model, measured on 44 arrays from 22 biological groups. Read them as a ranking, not as a probability that the class is correct.
